questions.q: In which state of matter do particles only vibrate about fixed positions?
questions.explanation: Particles of a solid are held in fixed positions and can only vibrate.

questions.q: Diffusion is fastest in
questions.explanation: Gas particles move freely with large spaces between them, so they mix fastest.

questions.q: The heat needed to change 1 kg of a solid into a liquid at its melting point is called the latent heat of
questions.explanation: This is the latent heat of fusion.

questions.q: Naphthalene balls kept in a cupboard slowly disappear without leaving any liquid. This is because they
questions.explanation: Naphthalene changes directly from solid to vapour.

questions.q: LPG can be supplied in small cylinders because gases can be
questions.explanation: Applying pressure turns a large volume of gas into a small volume of liquid.

questions.q: A gas fills the whole of its container, but a liquid does not, because gas particles
options: move freely in all directions and have negligible attraction between them
questions.explanation: With very weak attractions the particles spread to occupy all the space available.

questions.q: Water keeps boiling at 100 °C even though heat is supplied continuously, because
options: the heat supplied is used to change the liquid into vapour (latent heat)
the water loses all its heat to the pan
questions.explanation: The heat goes into overcoming particle attractions rather than raising the temperature.

questions.q: State two characteristics of the particles of matter.
questions.answer: The particles of matter are very small and have spaces between them. They are continuously moving, and they attract each other.
questions.explanation: These ideas explain diffusion and the three states of matter.

questions.q: Why do water droplets form on the outer surface of a glass containing ice-cold water?
questions.answer: Water vapour present in the air comes in contact with the cold surface of the glass and loses energy. It condenses into tiny droplets of liquid water on the outside of the glass.
questions.explanation: The water does not pass through the glass; it comes from the air.

questions.q: Soda water is an example of a solution of a
questions.explanation: Soda water has carbon dioxide gas dissolved in water.

questions.q: Which method can separate iron filings from sulphur powder when they are only mixed?
questions.explanation: Iron is attracted by a magnet but sulphur is not.

questions.q: A substance made up of only one kind of atom is a(n)
questions.explanation: An element contains only one kind of atom.

questions.q: Brass is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Brass is made from copper and zinc.

questions.q: 5 g of sugar is dissolved in 95 g of water. The mass percentage of sugar in the solution is
Which of these will scatter a beam of light passing through it?
questions.explanation: Starch solution is a colloid; the others are true solutions.

questions.q: To purify copper sulphate, crystallisation is preferred over simple evaporation to dryness because
options: crystallisation gives pure crystals and leaves impurities in the solution, while evaporation may leave impurities behind or decompose the solid
questions.explanation: On cooling a saturated solution pure crystals separate, while the impurities remain dissolved.

questions.q: What is chromatography? Give one use.
questions.answer: Chromatography is a method for separating the components of a mixture that dissolve in the same solvent, based on their different rates of movement over a paper or other material. It is used to separate dyes in ink or colours in a dye.
questions.explanation: Components that dissolve better in the solvent travel farther.

questions.q: Classify each of the following as an element, a compound or a mixture: sea water, hydrogen, sodium chloride, steel.
questions.answer: Sea water is a mixture. Hydrogen is an element. Sodium chloride is a compound. Steel is a mixture (an alloy of iron and carbon).
questions.explanation: Elements and compounds are pure substances; mixtures have two or more substances physically combined.

questions.q: The smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction is the
questions.explanation: The atom is the smallest particle of an element taking part in reactions.

questions.q: One atomic mass unit is defined as one-twelfth of the mass of a
questions.explanation: The standard for atomic mass is the carbon-12 atom.

questions.q: How many atoms are in a molecule of ozone, O3?
questions.explanation: The subscript 3 shows three oxygen atoms.

questions.q: The chemical formula of ammonia is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has valency 3 and hydrogen valency 1, so one N joins three H.

questions.q: How many atoms are present in one molecule of glucose, C6H12O6?
What is the mass of 6.022 × 10^23 molecules of water? (H = 1 u, O = 16 u)
questions.explanation: That number of molecules is one mole, which has a mass of 18 g.

questions.q: Which of the following has the greatest mass? (C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.explanation: Molar masses are 44, 32, 28 and 18 g respectively.

questions.q: Write the chemical symbols of calcium, copper, chlorine and nitrogen.
questions.answer: Calcium is Ca, copper is Cu, chlorine is Cl and nitrogen is N.
questions.explanation: Symbols may be one or two letters, with the first capital and the second small.

questions.q: On heating 10 g of calcium carbonate, 5.6 g of calcium oxide and 4.4 g of carbon dioxide are obtained. Which law does this verify? Explain.
questions.answer: It verifies the law of conservation of mass. The mass of the products is 5.6 + 4.4 = 10 g, which equals the mass of the reactant, so no mass is lost or gained.
questions.explanation: The total mass is the same before and after the reaction.

questions.q: The central part of an atom, containing protons and neutrons, is called the
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons are packed together in the nucleus.

questions.q: The overall electric charge on a neutral atom is
questions.explanation: The number of protons equals the number of electrons, so the charges cancel.

questions.q: In an atom, electrons are arranged in
questions.explanation: Electrons occupy shells around the nucleus.

questions.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of sodium with atomic number 11 and mass number 23?
questions.explanation: 23 − 11 = 12 neutrons.

questions.q: The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in the K shell is
questions.explanation: 2n² with n = 1 gives 2.

questions.q: An element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 8, 2. Its valency is
questions.explanation: It has two electrons in the outermost shell, which it can lose.

questions.q: Which pair of atoms (atomic number, mass number) are isotopes of the same element?
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number (17) but different mass numbers.

questions.q: State two uses of isotopes.
questions.answer: An isotope of uranium is used as a fuel in nuclear reactors. An isotope of cobalt is used in the treatment of cancer, and an isotope of iodine is used in the treatment of goitre.
questions.explanation: Any two valid uses are acceptable.

questions.q: Why does the atomic number, and not the mass number, identify an element?
questions.answer: The atomic number is the number of protons, which is fixed for each element. Atoms of the same element can have different mass numbers (isotopes), and atoms of different elements can have the same mass number (isobars), so mass number cannot identify an element.
keyPoints: Atomic number is the number of protons
questions.explanation: Only the proton number is the same for all atoms of one element.

questions.q: Which of the following is a unicellular organism?
questions.explanation: Amoeba consists of a single cell.

questions.q: The nucleus is surrounded by a double-layered covering called the
questions.explanation: The nuclear membrane has pores for the exchange of materials.

questions.q: Vacuoles in plant cells are filled with
options: cell sap containing water, sugars and wastes
questions.explanation: The large vacuole stores water, sugars, amino acids and waste substances.

questions.q: Which organelle is found in both plant and animal cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria occur in both kinds of cells.

questions.q: The endoplasmic reticulum serves as
options: a channel for transport of materials within the cell
a store of the cell's DNA
questions.explanation: ER is a network of membranes that carries materials through the cytoplasm.

questions.q: The plasma membrane is made mainly of
questions.explanation: It is organised as a layer of lipids with proteins.

questions.q: Onion peel cells are placed in a strong salt solution. The cell contents shrink away from the cell wall because
options: the cell absorbs water and bursts
water leaves the cell by osmosis
salt enters and makes the cell divide
questions.explanation: Water moves out into the more concentrated solution, and the protoplasm shrinks (plasmolysis).

questions.q: What is diffusion? Give an example of its importance in cells.
questions.answer: Diffusion is the spontaneous movement of a substance from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration. For example, oxygen diffuses into the cell and carbon dioxide diffuses out of the cell.
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the main way in which gases are exchanged by cells.

questions.q: Why is the cell called the structural and functional unit of life?
questions.answer: All living organisms are made of cells, so the cell is the structural unit. Each cell can carry out the basic functions of life such as taking in food, respiration and removing wastes, so it is also the functional unit.
keyPoints: Cell is the smallest living unit
questions.explanation: Even single cells such as amoeba perform all life processes.

questions.q: Which of the following is a permanent tissue?
questions.explanation: Parenchyma is a simple permanent tissue; the others are meristems.

questions.q: Intercalary meristem is found
options: at the base of leaves or internodes
questions.explanation: It adds length at the base of leaves and internodes, as in grasses.

questions.q: Phloem transports
questions.explanation: Phloem carries sugars made by photosynthesis to all parts of the plant.

questions.q: Ciliated epithelium in the windpipe helps to
options: move mucus and dust out of the respiratory tract
questions.explanation: The cilia beat to push mucus and trapped particles out.

questions.q: Which muscle is found only in the heart?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle forms the wall of the heart.

questions.q: The wood of a tree trunk consists mainly of
questions.explanation: Wood is mostly xylem that has built up over the years.

questions.q: The tall, pillar-like epithelial cells that line the intestine are suited to
questions.explanation: Columnar epithelium helps movement of substances across the lining.

questions.q: State two functions of areolar tissue.
questions.answer: Areolar tissue fills the space inside organs and supports internal organs. It also helps in the repair of tissues.
questions.explanation: It is a connective tissue found between the skin and muscles and around organs.

questions.q: How is the structure of sclerenchyma suited to its function?
questions.answer: Sclerenchyma cells are dead and have thick walls hardened with lignin, and there is almost no space between the cells. This makes the tissue strong and rigid, so it gives mechanical support to the plant.
keyPoints: Dead cells with thick lignified walls
questions.explanation: Structure and function are matched in each tissue.

questions.q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed has magnitude only; the others have direction too.

questions.q: Motion in which the velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time is called
questions.explanation: Constant acceleration means equal velocity changes in equal times.

questions.q: A passenger sitting in a moving train is at rest relative to
questions.explanation: Rest and motion are relative; the passenger does not change position with respect to the train.

questions.q: A speed of 54 km/h is equal to
How long does a body moving at 5 m/s take to cover 150 m?
On a distance-time graph the line for body A is steeper than the line for body B. This means
options: both move at the same speed
questions.explanation: A steeper slope means a greater speed.

questions.q: A car's velocity changes from 10 m/s to 20 m/s in 5 s. Its average acceleration is
What does the slope of a distance-time graph represent? What does the graph of a body at rest look like?
questions.answer: The slope of a distance-time graph represents the speed of the body. For a body at rest the distance does not change with time, so the graph is a straight line parallel to the time axis.
questions.explanation: A steeper line means a faster body.

questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s. Find the maximum height it reaches and the time taken to reach it. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer: At the highest point v = 0 and a = −10 m/s². From v = u + at: 0 = 20 − 10t, so t = 2 s. From v² = u² + 2as: 0 = 400 − 20s, so s = 20 m.
questions.explanation: Upward motion is retarded by gravity.

questions.q: A ball rolling on level ground slows down and stops because of
questions.explanation: Friction opposes the motion and slows the ball.

questions.q: Newton's second law relates the force on a body to its
questions.explanation: F = ma.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of the inertia of motion?
options: A book stays at rest on a table
A coin falls into a glass when the card under it is flicked
Dust falls out when a carpet is beaten
A passenger leans forward when a moving bus brakes suddenly
questions.explanation: The passenger's body tends to continue moving forward.

questions.q: A force of 12 N acts on a 3 kg body. The acceleration produced is
A force of 5 N acts on a body for 2 s. The change in its momentum is
questions.explanation: Change in momentum = force × time = 5 × 2 = 10 kg m/s.

questions.q: The same force acts on a 2 kg body and on a 4 kg body. The acceleration of the 2 kg body is
options: the same as that of the 4 kg body
half that of the 4 kg body
twice that of the 4 kg body
four times that of the 4 kg body
questions.explanation: a = F / m, so half the mass gives twice the acceleration.

questions.q: A 2 kg cart moving at 3 m/s collides with a stationary 1 kg cart and the two stick together. Their common velocity is
Give two examples of Newton's third law in everyday life.
questions.answer: When we walk, we push the ground backward and the ground pushes us forward. When a balloon releases air backward, the air pushes the balloon forward. A rocket and the recoil of a gun are also examples.
questions.explanation: Any two correct examples with the action and reaction identified are acceptable.

questions.q: A force of 6 N acts on a body of mass 2 kg initially at rest. Find its velocity and the distance travelled after 4 s.
questions.answer: Acceleration a = 6 / 2 = 3 m/s². Velocity v = at = 3 × 4 = 12 m/s. Distance s = ½at² = ½ × 3 × 16 = 24 m.
questions.explanation: Find a from F = ma, then use the equations of motion.

questions.q: The Moon stays in its orbit around the Earth because of the
questions.explanation: The Earth's gravitational pull provides the centripetal force.

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity at a place does not depend on the
questions.explanation: g = GM/R², which has no term for the falling object's mass.

questions.q: The weight of a 50 kg person on Earth is about (g = 9.8 m/s²)
Relative density of a substance
questions.explanation: It is the ratio of two densities, so the units cancel.

questions.q: We do not notice the gravitational force between everyday objects because
options: the value of G is extremely small
the objects are always far apart
the force between them is repulsive
questions.explanation: G is about 6.67 × 10^-11 N m²/kg², so the force between small masses is tiny.

questions.q: When an object is taken from the ground to the top of a very high mountain, its weight
questions.explanation: g decreases slightly with height, so the weight decreases a little.

questions.q: Distinguish between the universal gravitational constant G and the acceleration due to gravity g.
questions.answer: G is a constant with the same value everywhere in the universe (6.67 × 10^-11 N m²/kg²). The value of g is about 9.8 m/s² on the surface of the Earth and changes from place to place, for example with height and on other planets.
keyPoints: g varies from place to place
questions.explanation: g depends on G, the mass and the radius of the planet.

questions.q: An object weighs 10 N on the Earth. Find its mass and its weight on the Moon, where gravity is one-sixth of the Earth's. (g = 10 m/s² on Earth)
questions.answer: Mass = weight / g = 10 / 10 = 1 kg, which is the same on the Moon. Weight on the Moon = 10 / 6 = about 1.67 N.
questions.explanation: Only the weight, not the mass, changes with gravity.

questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Wind is replenished naturally; fossil fuels are not.

questions.q: The work done by a force is zero when the displacement of the body is
questions.explanation: Work = force × displacement, so zero displacement gives zero work.

questions.q: The formula for the kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with speed v is
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv².

questions.q: The kinetic energy of a 1000 kg car moving at 10 m/s is
A loudspeaker converts
questions.explanation: A loudspeaker turns electrical signals into sound.

questions.q: A weightlifter holds a 50 kg weight steady above his head for 10 s. The work done on the weight during this time is
questions.explanation: There is no displacement of the weight, so no work is done on it.

questions.q: Give two examples of energy transformation in daily life.
questions.answer: In an electric bulb electrical energy changes into light and heat. In a battery-run toy, chemical energy changes into electrical and then into kinetic energy. A burning candle changes chemical energy into heat and light.
keyPoints: One example with both forms named
A second example with both forms named
questions.explanation: Any two correct transformations are acceptable.

questions.q: Person A lifts a 20 kg bag through 3 m in 10 s and person B does the same in 20 s. Compare the work done and the power of the two persons.
questions.answer: The work done is the same for both, mgh = 20 × g × 3. Power is work divided by time, so A, who takes half the time, has twice the power of B.
keyPoints: A has twice the power of B
questions.explanation: Power depends on how fast the work is done.

questions.q: Sound waves require
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a medium.

questions.q: The loudness of a sound depends mainly on its
questions.explanation: A larger amplitude gives a louder sound.

questions.q: The SI unit of wavelength is the
questions.explanation: Wavelength is a length.

questions.q: The quality (timbre) of a sound allows us to
options: distinguish two sounds of the same pitch and loudness
questions.explanation: Timbre is the feature that makes a guitar sound different from a flute.

questions.q: A rarefaction in a sound wave is a region of
questions.explanation: In a rarefaction the particles are spread out, so the pressure is low.

questions.q: A sound wave has a frequency of 500 Hz and a wavelength of 0.68 m. Its speed is
Explain why sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
questions.answer: Sound travels as vibrations of the particles of a medium, which pass the disturbance from one particle to the next as compressions and rarefactions. In a vacuum there are no particles, so the sound cannot be carried.
questions.explanation: This is shown by a ringing bell in a jar from which the air is pumped out.

questions.q: Two instruments play the same note at the same loudness, yet we can tell them apart. Explain.
questions.answer: The two sounds have the same pitch (frequency) and the same loudness (amplitude), but they differ in quality or timbre because the waveforms are different. The timbre helps us to tell the sound of one instrument from another.
questions.explanation: Timbre arises from the mixture of frequencies in the sound.

questions.q: Which of the following is a micronutrient needed by plants?
questions.explanation: Iron is needed in small quantities, so it is a micronutrient.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fodder crop?
questions.explanation: Berseem is grown as fodder for animals.

questions.q: Sericulture is the rearing of silkworms for
questions.explanation: Silkworms are reared to obtain silk fibre.

questions.q: Exotic breeds such as Jersey are crossed with local breeds of cattle mainly to improve
questions.explanation: Crossing combines the high milk yield of exotic breeds with the hardiness of local breeds.

questions.q: The purpose of crop protection management is to
options: protect crops from weeds, insects and diseases
questions.explanation: Crop protection saves crops from the factors that reduce yield.

questions.q: Weeds reduce the yield of a crop because they compete with it for
questions.explanation: Weeds use the same resources that the crop needs.

questions.q: What is animal husbandry?
questions.answer: Animal husbandry is the scientific management of livestock. It includes feeding, breeding and the disease control of animals to get products such as milk, eggs and meat.
questions.explanation: Good husbandry increases both the quantity and quality of animal products.

questions.q: A farmer finds many weeds in his wheat field. Suggest two methods of controlling them and explain why controlling them matters.
questions.answer: Weeds can be removed by hand or with tools (weeding) and by spraying weedicides in the correct amount. They must be controlled because weeds compete with the crop for nutrients, water and light and so reduce the yield.
questions.explanation: Weedicides should be used carefully so as not to harm the crop or the environment.
